cohort: 347 mothers with children greater than or equal to 2 years old in Worabe town, Ethiopia
finding: Less than half of the mothers (42.1%) practiced optimal breastfeeding, with several factors influencing this practice, including maternal occupation, household income, knowledge of optimal breastfeeding, access to breastfeeding counselling and antenatal care, and mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Mothers who had a caesarean section delivery were more likely to practice optimal breastfeeding (AOR = 4.2, 95% CI: 1.2, 14.1).
